data.title: NLC India's green energy arm to pursue USD-355m listing
data.description:
November 20 (Renewables Now) - NLC India Renewables, the green energy arm of state-owned coal miner and power producer NLC India Ltd (BOM:513683), has filed draft papers for an INR-33-billion (USD 354.9m/EUR 323.1m) initial public offering (IPO).

The parent company said on Thursday that a draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) for the contemplated transaction was filed with India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

Through a fresh issue of shares, trading will be pursued on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited, formerly Bombay Stock Exchange. The deal will also include an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 100 million shares in NLC India Renewables by promoter NLC India Ltd.

The proposed IPO is pending regulatory clearance and is subject to prevailing market conditions and other considerations. It will be managed by SBI Capital Markets, HDFC Bank, IDBI Capital Markets and Securities and IIFL Capital Services. Proceeds raised from the sale will be allocated to repay NLC India Renewables’ debt, with a portion of the funds to go for general corporate requirements.

NLC India Renewables develops, builds and operates renewable power plants and sells their output under long-term deals with central and state government agencies and public utilities.

As of end-October, the firm's portfolio consisted of 7.2 GW of solar, wind, hybrid and firm and dispatchable renewable energy capacity, including 1.78 GW in operation, and 3.58 GWh of battery storage. Its project pipeline for power generation and storage capacity amounted to 9 GW and 4.66 GWh, respectively. The company has also been expanding into pumped storage and green hydrogen.

(INR 10 = USD 0.108/EUR 0.098)

data.title: Qben Infra: B45 Anlegg Selected for NOK 28 Million Contract to Rehabilitate Critical Hydropower Infrastructure
data.description:
Qben Infra AB (publ) announces that its subsidiary B45 Anlegg AS, part of the Qben Power business area, has been selected as the preferred bidder for a contract with Skafså Kraftverk ANS for the rehabilitation of Dam Hylebuhylen in Tokke municipality, Telemark, Norway. The award recommendation is based on B45 Anlegg having submitted the most economically advantageous tender.

The contract value is estimated at approximately NOK 28 million, with project commencement scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

The dam forms part of Norway's critical infrastructure for hydropower generation. The rehabilitation works will contribute to ensuring long-term operational reliability, dam safety and a secure supply of electricity.

The project further strengthens B45 Anlegg's position as a contractor within critical infrastructure and supports Qben Infra's strategic focus on the energy and power sector.

Hydropower plays a central role in Norway's energy supply, and the need for maintenance, rehabilitation and modernisation of existing hydropower infrastructure is expected to create significant market opportunities in the years ahead.

Project information:

  • Project: Dam Hylebuhylen
  • Client: Skafså Kraftverk ANS
  • Municipality: Tokke
  • County: Telemark
  • Contract value: Approximately NOK 28 million
  • Scheduled commencement: Q1 2027

The deadline for submitting appeals is 3 December 2026. The award recommendation remains subject to final contract execution.

E-mail: anders.kjoll@qpower.no

data.title: Asia tech stocks reel from Anthropic IPO as SoftBank, Samsung, and TSMC slide
data.description:
• Shares of Japan’s SoftBank Group tumbled 16.16% on Friday, amid a broader decline in Asian technology stocks following the much-anticipated stock market debut of Anthropic . 
  • SoftBank, one of the biggest backers of OpenAI , Anthropic’s rival, with a total investment of $64.6B in the ChatGPT maker, suffered the worst day in over two years.
  • Additionally, the company's ownership of chip designer Arm has made its shares particularly sensitive to shifts in sentiment toward the AI sector. The stock lost 30% in October and is down 31% so far this month.
  • Japanese semiconductor stocks also tumbled, with Tokyo Electron dropping 7.06%, Lasertec down 9.21%, and Renesas Electronics losing 7.02%.
  • The sell-off extended to South Korea, where Nvidia suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics fell 5.92% and 7.01%, respectively, pressuring the benchmark Kospi, which ended 5.21% lower.
  • Meanwhile in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC , closed 4.76% lower in Taiwan. Elsewhere, Chinese tech giant Tencent fell 2.01%, while memory chipmaker CXMT slid 5.31% to a record low. Baidu declined 4.79%, while AI chipmaker Enflame, regarded as one of China’s “four little dragons,” dropped 7.16%.

data.title: Poland's Grupa Azoty says Europe to remain high-cost nitrogen market in Q4
data.description:
Polish fertilizer and chemicals maker Grupa Azoty expects Europe to remain a high-cost nitrogen fertilizer market in the fourth quarter, it said in a quarterly report on Thursday, after the Iran war sent gas prices soaring, pushing its agricultural segment to a loss.

Azoty said the outlook for the coming quarters remained challenging, though a seasonal pickup in fertilizer demand was possible before spring, with the scale depending on farmers’ finances and fertilizer prices.

  • Fertilizer price rises lagged raw material costs, and many farmers held back purchases, leaving much seasonal demand unmet going into Q4, Azoty said

  • High gas prices are forcing some European urea producers to cut capacity, and Azoty sees a risk of urea prices rising sharply in early 2027

  • Forecasts point to urea oversupply returning by the end of March, provided shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains stable, it said

  • High costs add strain on state-controlled Azoty, which said in September it lacked funds for major investment until its debt was restructured

  • Azoty's Q3 net loss widened to 547.2 million zlotys ($135.4 million) from 149.8 million a year ago, as previously communicated

($1 = 4.0423 zlotys)

data.title: U.K. Government Borrowed More in October, But Stays on Track for Smaller Deficit — Update
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

The U.K. government borrowed more in October than a year earlier, but it remained on course to reduce its budget deficit in the current fiscal year.

The Office for National Statistics on Friday said government spending exceeded revenues by 17 billion pounds ($22.25 billion) in October, an increase of 800 million pounds from the same month of 2025.

The increase in borrowing partly reflected a rise in interest costs as inflation and bond yields picked up since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

In October, interest payments totaled 11.2 billion pounds, an increase of 2.8 billion pounds from the same month last year.

"Much of the deficit is out of the government's control, with the war in the Middle East continuing to put pressure on inflation and the economy," said Kit Rees, an investment strategist at Quilter.

Over the first seven months of the fiscal year that will end in early April, borrowing was 111.3 billion pounds, down 7.3 billion pounds from the same period a year earlier.

At 3.5% of gross domestic product, the budget deficit for the fiscal year to October was lower than the 3.8% recorded a year earlier.

The government's total debt stood at 3.1 trillion pounds, or 95.8% of GDP, up from 93.9% in October 2025.

In its October budget, the government set out plans for spending and taxation that aim to reduce the budget deficit further in the current and subsequent fiscal years. However, borrowing is set to be higher than previously targeted.

For this year, the Office for Budget Responsibility estimates the budget deficit will be 4.2% of gross domestic product, a large increase from the 3.6% planned in March.

The overshoot partly reflects the increased costs of providing government services as energy prices have risen since the start of the war. Higher prices are also raising the cost of paying interest, since the U.K. has a higher share of bonds with payouts linked to inflation than its peers.

Write to Paul Hannon at paul.hannon@wsj.com

data.title: Gold set for worst week in eight months as firm dollar, Fed hike bets weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold eyes biggest weekly fall since March
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly declines
  • Fed's Paulson says Fed will need to raise rates again

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices slipped on Friday and were headed for their worst week in eight months, as a resilient US dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December weighed on bullion.

Spot gold fell 1.9% to $3,552.39 per ounce by 0730 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. Bullion was down about 8.5% so far this week, its sharpest weekly decline since the week ending March 20.

US gold futures for December delivery slid 3.6% to $3,553.10.

"There seems to be a bit of forced liquidation going on across the market in general, with expectations of imminent US rate hikes and inflation that could be persistent, leading to high yields and a higher US dollar as a result, pressuring gold," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

Asian shares were on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AI sector.

The dollar held near a 19-month high, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for holders of other currencies.

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets see a 99.3% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in India and China strengthened this week as the price slump lured bargain hunters, while investors in China viewed the correction as a buying opportunity.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 2.4% to $41.73 per ounce, platinum dropped 3.1% to $1,302.45, and palladium slid 2.5% to $886.86. All three metals were headed for weekly losses.

data.title: India's AI-free appeal draws record foreign buying, earnings will decide if it lasts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Foreign investors put record $12 billion into stocks in November
  • India gives emerging-market exposure insulated from AI swings
  • Nifty 50 rises over 11% this month, outperforming Asian peers
  • Earnings growth at four-year high
  • Whether India shift lasts depends on earnings, strategists say

By Jaspreet Kalra, Bharath Rajeswaran and Ankur Banerjee

Foreign investors are returning to India at a record rate in search of shelter from the fickle AI trade that has convulsed global markets, two years after pulling their money to ride the AI wave in countries central to the AI supply chain.

Whether they stay, however, depends on if newly revived earnings growth can last, strategists and fund managers said.

Foreigners have poured $12 billion into shares so far in November, the largest-ever monthly inflow, compared with more than $60 billion of selling from September 2024 to October 2026.

Those investors have enjoyed the blue-chip Nifty 50 index climbing over 11% this month. That compared with benchmarks in AI centres South Korea and Taiwan, which are down more than 15%, and the US, where the Nasdaq index is down 6%.

What held India back for two years is now what makes it attractive. With India lacking major AI bets, investors pumped money into markets blessed with companies along the AI value chain. However, that lack has since made India a haven as investors question the potential returns on massive debt-fuelled spending on AI-related infrastructure and software.

India may not have AI appeal, but the reverse can also be attractive, said Alexander Redman, chief equity strategist at brokerage CITIC CLSA, drawing on the carrot-and-stick analogy.

For those investing in India, the stick is the need to diversify from tech-heavy markets, while the carrot is India's own attractions such as improving earnings growth, Redman said.

"At the moment, I think the stick is bigger than the carrot," he said.

The pivot has helped the equity market reclaim its place among the world's top five by market capitalisation.

India had dropped down the ranking as soft economic expansion and a weak rupee slowed earnings growth, but a robust economy and a stabilising currency this year have propelled earnings in dollar terms.

Aberdeen increased exposure to two large asset managers over the past three months, saying improved valuations and earnings growth have raised the market's appeal.

India has "a combination of OK valuations and earnings growth coming back - that's a reasonable setup," said Isaac Thong, Aberdeen's senior investment director for Asian equities.

Ashmore and Artemis Fund Managers have also increased Indian exposure. For the first time since January, investors who are overweight India outnumber those who are underweight, a BofA survey conducted this month showed.

India has also benefited from being one of the largest and most liquid emerging markets amid the rush away from tech-heavy South Korea and Taiwan.

Portfolio manager Todd McClone at William Blair Investment Management has cut exposure to the tech sector to add Indian stocks, favouring financial, healthcare and consumer firms.

McClone said much of the emerging-market universe has become a leveraged bet on AI hyperscaler spending, and "India gives investors exposure to EM growth that isn't tied to that cycle."

The variance was on display on Friday as Mumbai stocks (.dMIIN00000PUS) were the sole gainers in Asia as AI worries drove down regional stocks (.MIAP00000PUS) by more than 3%.

TACTICAL TRADE

An inflection in earnings bolsters the case for revisiting India. The country's 50 biggest firms posted their strongest profit growth in more than four years for the September quarter, prompting analysts to raise earnings forecasts.

US dollar-denominated earnings per share, a gauge of earnings growth for foreign investors, has turned higher for the first time in two years, Redman said.

"We need more confidence that it (earnings growth) is sustainable. You need to basically see those earnings revisions get positive. If that happens, this will be longer than a tactical trade," Redman said.

Brokerages including Goldman Sachs, Citi, HSBC, TS Lombard and Bernstein have also turned more bullish on India.

Global equity funds are underweight on India and bringing allocations in line with benchmark weights could translate into inflows of around $115 billion, JPMorgan said in a client note last month.

DEGREES OF CAUTION

Lower oil prices and measures to stabilise the rupee have also eased pressure, though both are vulnerable to developments in the US-Iran conflict.

A sustained decline in the rupee reduces dollar returns for foreign investors, while higher oil prices widen India's import bill and increase demand for dollars, pressuring the currency and deterring capital inflows.

There is also doubt about whether recent buying represents a lasting shift in sentiment toward India or a response to developments elsewhere. Uncertainty regarding the impact of developments in AI on India also lingers.

"We do not yet see a durable shift in investors' longer-term view of India," said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, whose firm is overweight in the market.

"Many remain concerned that advances in AI could disrupt India's labour-intensive service industries, potentially weighing on employment, income growth and the broader consumption story."

Artemis has selectively increased exposure to Indian stocks in emerging-market equities fund but is not moving towards a benchmark-weight or overweight position, said Raheel Altaf, fund manager for the firm's Global Emerging Markets Equity fund.

"Our view is that we need to be a little more patient, but certainly the number of opportunities in the Indian market has gone up quite a bit," Altaf said.
